overview: The committee reviewed the Preliminary Design Program (PDP) submission status, featuring a detailed space summary and initial comparative cost estimates for 29 design alternatives ranging from $850 million to $935 million.

items.title: Meeting Minutes
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes for the January 14 full committee meeting and the January 28 communications subcommittee meeting.

items.title: Communications and Community Engagement Plan
items.summary: Approved a communications plan featuring a new mailing list, flyers with QR codes, micro-videos produced by vocational students, and citywide mailer options. The plan aims to inform residents of project milestones and engagement opportunities through June.

items.title: Financial Approvals and Contract Amendments
items.summary: Approved January 2026 invoices totaling $141,900 and a $17,600 contract amendment for independent estimating services. The amendment reallocates existing feasibility funds for independent cost verification during the preliminary design phases.

items.title: Preliminary Design Program (PDP) Status and Space Summary
items.summary: Reviewed the space summary required for the February 25 PDP submission, comparing proposed school dimensions against state guidelines for classrooms, labs, and vocational shops. Discussion focused on the educational rationale for 950-square-foot classrooms and expanded Chapter 74 vocational programming.

items.title: Comparative Cost Analysis of Design Alternatives
items.summary: Presented initial cost estimates for 29 design options, with total projected costs ranging from approximately $850 million to $935 million. These high-level estimates include direct trade costs, soft costs, construction contingencies, and escalation to the 2028 midpoint of construction.

items.title: Program Alternates and Site Priorities
items.summary: Evaluated the financial and spatial impacts of program alternates including a new Early Childhood Center, parking structures, and pool renovation versus new construction. The committee also discussed HVAC alternatives, comparing geothermal systems against air-source heat pump options.

items.title: Benchmarking and Reimbursement Motion
items.summary: Tabled and eventually failed a motion to request additional benchmarking data against Waltham and Somerville schools and formal reimbursement range estimates. Opponents argued the request was outside the current scope and that direct comparisons to other districts were premature or arbitrary.

subject: MSBA Preliminary Design Program and Cost Estimates
